summary: feat(sync): fill the temporal-filter mapping so --since and the stored watermark send lastModifiedGe (issue #13)
reason: sync --since and the stored last_synced_at watermark were both inert: the generated syncResourceSinceParam / syncResourceSinceParamFormat switches were EMPTY (the printer only emits them from an x-pp-sync-since hint the Fiken spec does not carry), so both walkers hit the 'endpoint declares no temporal filter' branch for every resource, dropped the window, emitted sync_warning reason=resource_not_incremental and re-pulled every page of every resource for every company on every run - about 1500 sequential requests for the four-company mirror behind a one-request flock (issue #13). The API does support it: spec.yaml declares the shared components.parameters.lastModifiedGe (type string, format date, YYYY-MM-DD, INCLUSIVE) on exactly five of the synced list operations - getContacts (:718), getJournalEntries (:1131), getTransactions (:1274), getProducts (:2770), getSales (:2914) - and the payloads carry a matching lastModifiedDate. (getInvoices :1381, getCreditNotes :1815 and getTimeEntries :4082 declare it too but are not sync resources.) purchases declares no filter and carries no lastModifiedDate; accounts, bank_accounts, companies, inbox and projects declare no date filter at all. Those five keep the resource_not_incremental warning and a full pull, unchanged and asserted. THE MAPPING goes into the generated switches, not into the hand-authored resolver seam, because the pair IS the printed data table for this: a reprint that ever learns the parameter should collide with it in the diff rather than silently disagree with a mapping hidden elsewhere. Both arms are marked PATCH(sync-since-last-modified) and the seams syncSinceParamFor / syncSinceParamFormatFor still delegate to them. THE VALUE is not the raw watermark. lastModifiedGe compares a DAY, so a time-of-day suffix is not a valid value at all, and the day it compares against carries no zone. syncSinceWindowValue (internal/cli/sync_since.go) therefore floors the value to its day (formatSyncSinceValue's existing 'date' arm) and then steps back ONE day. The floor is forced by the format; the extra day is the margin the day granularity costs - the client's local day boundary is not the one the API stamped the row with, the watermark is written when a run ENDS while rows keep changing during it, and client and server clocks need not agree. Cost: at most two days of rows re-upserted per incremental run, which is idempotent; the failure it prevents (a row modified during the run, never seen again) is permanent. A format this function does not understand is passed through unchanged, so a future timestamp filter is not silently widened. It is applied at the single formatting site in each walker, so --since and the watermark path get the same treatment.  CORRECTION (review follow-up, same record): the "automatic watermark path" this reason first claimed is INERT for every shipped resource, and the text above must be read with that in mind. sync_state.last_synced_at is read in exactly one place, syncResource, which walks flat resources - and `companies` is the only flat resource this CLI has, and it declares no date filter - so the watermark is always dropped by the resource_not_incremental branch before it can become a window. The five resources that DO declare lastModifiedGe (contacts, journal_entries, transactions, products, sales) are all walked by syncDependentResource, which never reads last_synced_at at all and could not apply it per company if it did, because sync_state is keyed by resource_type alone. In production only an explicit --since windows a pull; a default `fiken-cli sync` is still a full pull of every resource, and that is what the doc comments in sync_since.go and the PATCH comments in sync.go now say. A per-(company, resource) watermark is a schema change, out of scope here, and filed separately. ALSO, and this one was a data-loss hazard: --full and --since are now REFUSED TOGETHER at flag validation in newSyncCmd (usage error, exit 2, before a client or the mirror is opened). `sync --full --company S --resources R --since 7d` ran clearFullSyncCompanyRows - a real DELETE of every row of that (company, resource) - and then refetched only lastModifiedGe=<today-8d>, because the dependent walker takes sinceTS unconditionally and never consults its `full` parameter. Every row outside the window was deleted and never fetched back. Rejecting the pair at the flag layer is the minimal fix and keeps the walkers oblivious; --full alone still ignores the (inert) watermark. THE WINDOW IS A VALUE, not a bare flag: windowedPull / depWindowedPull are now syncPullWindow {Param, Value, Windowed} built by newSyncPullWindow, the request reads Param/Value, shouldRecordResultCount reads Windowed (a windowed pull gets the FILTERED Fiken-Api-Result-Count back and must never overwrite the full-collection number recorded beside sync_state.total_count - issue #15's reason for the flag, now reachable in production rather than only from a test), and AllowsDeletion() is the contract issue #17's deletion pass must consult: a pull that asked for the rows changed since a date cannot conclude that an absent row is gone. The per-pull result_count_mismatch comparison still runs for a windowed pull, because header and rows describe the same filtered set. OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately: no cursor or watermark persistence changes. --since is a window the caller supplies, which is how nOracle drives it; the issue's 'related gap' (sync_state keyed by resource_type alone, so the watermark is mirror-wide rather than per (company, resource), and a dependent sync interrupted at company 3 of 4 restarts at company 1 page 0) is a separate change and stays open. Until it lands, the automatic watermark path is only correct for a single-company mirror or a full re-pull; --since and --full are the controls a multi-company caller should use. USER-FACING NOTE (the README/SKILL line is deferred to the orchestrator, which holds those files): `fiken-cli sync --since 7d` now really does ask Fiken for only what changed, for contacts, journal_entries, transactions, products and sales - the window is sent as lastModifiedGe with the start day floored and moved back one day, so a run re-pulls a day or two of already-seen rows rather than risk missing one. accounts, bank_accounts, companies, inbox, projects and purchases have no date filter on their Fiken endpoints: they are still pulled in full and each says so once with reason=resource_not_incremental. An incremental run deliberately does not update the recorded result_count, because the API's count describes the window, not the collection.
call_sites: func newSyncPullWindow(param, value string, userParams *syncUserParams, resource string, isDependent bool) syncPullWindow {
windowedPull := newSyncPullWindow(sinceParam, effectiveSince, userParams, resource, false)
depWindowedPull := newSyncPullWindow(depSinceParam, depSinceTS, userParams, dep.Name, true)
return usageErr(fmt.Errorf("--full and --since cannot be combined: --full refetches every row, --since only a window"))
"Full resync (ignore previous checkpoint). Cannot be combined with --since."
"Incremental sync duration (e.g. 7d, 24h, 1w, 30m). Cannot be combined with --full."
validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh) plus go test -race ./internal/cli/.... Hand-authored tests in internal/cli/sync_since_test.go, on the httptest rowServer/pageServer harness: TestSyncResourceSinceParam_MapsOnlyTheFilteredResources pins the data table both ways (five resources map to lastModifiedGe/date, the other six to "" - sending a synthetic parameter to them would be a 400); TestSyncSinceWindowValue_FloorsToDayAndStepsBackOne pins the value rule including month and year boundaries and the two pass-through cases; TestSyncPullWindow_WindowedPullForbidsDeletion pins the issue #17 contract, including a --resource-param pull that is windowed with no since value; TestSyncDependentResource_SinceSendsDayFlooredLastModifiedGe drives a real --since 7d contacts pull and asserts lastModifiedGe equals (now-7d floored, minus one) on every request with no other date parameter and no warning; TestSyncDependentResource_UnmappedResourceStillWarnsNotIncremental asserts accounts sends no date parameter and emits exactly one resource_not_incremental naming itself; TestSyncDependentResource_WindowedPullKeepsRecordedResultCount asserts a windowed short pull still emits one result_count_mismatch while the recorded 577 survives; TestSyncResource_WatermarkArmFloorsThroughAFakeResolver drives the watermark arm (sync_state last_synced_at set, no --since) through FAKE resolver seams on companies, because no shipped resource reaches that arm, and asserts the derived window and that --full sends none; TestSyncDependentResource_DefaultRunIsAFullPull pins the honest behaviour instead - contacts with a stored watermark and no --since sends no date parameter at all; TestSync_FullWithSinceIsARejectedCombination drives the real sync command and asserts exit code 2, the usage message, zero HTTP requests and two surviving sales rows for the scoped company. Every new test was checked red against the pre-fix code (empty switch, and separately without the minus-one-day step). The existing TestSyncResource_WindowedPullKeepsRecordedResultCount and TestSyncResource_ResourceParamPullKeepsRecordedResultCount still pass unchanged. No live API call was made and no fiken write command was run.
